extracted.intended_audience: researchers seeking mental-health research funding; donors and general public interested in foundation grants
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Brain & Behavior Research Foundation's grant program: mission, funding focus (mental-illness research), selection process (scientific council review), donation allocation, award frequency, and historical funding by disorder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research selection by Scientific Council
rubrics_metrics.description: We only award grants to scientists whose research is reviewed and selected by our world-renowned Scientific Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies that grant applications are evaluated and chosen via review by the Foundation's Scientific Council (peer/expert selection). Page emphasizes 'world-renowned scientists' as reviewers; no further selection criteria or scoring rubric provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding focus: cutting-edge research to find cures for mental illness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Brain & Behavior Research Foundation is committed to alleviating the suffering caused by mental illness by awarding scientific research grants that will ultimately enable people to live full, happy and productive lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the program's substantive mission and priority: support scientific research aimed at understanding and curing mental illness. This frames eligible work as 'cutting-edge' research targeting mental-health disorders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donation allocation transparency — 100% of donations for research goes to research
rubrics_metrics.description: 100% of Donations for Research Goes to Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site states: '100% of your contributions for research are invested in our grants to scientists thanks to the generous support of two family foundations which cover our operating expenses.' This is an organizational funding-policy criterion — donors' research-designated contributions are applied entirely to grants rather than overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant award frequency / timing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural scheduling detail for the program (three award cycles per year). The page also notes 'Total dollars awarded are updated annually.' No application deadlines or cycle dates provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority disorder/area funding history
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists historical dollars awarded by disorder (e.g., Schizophrenia $178M, Depression $131.7M, Autism $22.9M, Addiction $17.2M, PTSD $15.4M, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page presents cumulative funding amounts since 1987 for various mental-health categories, implying the Foundation's areas of emphasis and past investment priorities. This is historical/prioritization information rather than an explicit application scoring criterion.
